sources.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: 66-year-old man Preferred language: English Admission date: 10/03/2026 Discharge date: 10/08/2026 Admission diagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke, left MCA territory

Discharge diagnoses:

Acute ischemic stroke, left MCA territory (minor stroke, NIHSS 3 on admission, 1 at discharge)
Hypertension, uncontrolled
Hyperlipidemia
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Tobacco use disorder
Cocaine use disorder
Hospital Course Patient presented within 6 hours of onset of right hand weakness and word-finding difficulty. CT head negative for hemorrhage. Not a thrombolysis candidate due to rapidly improving, non-disabling deficits. MRI brain confirmed small acute infarct in the left MCA territory. CTA head/neck without large-vessel occlusion or significant carotid stenosis. TTE with bubble study: normal LVEF, no thrombus, no PFO. Telemetry without atrial fibrillation; 14-day ambulatory cardiac monitor placed prior to discharge to evaluate for paroxysmal AF.

Loaded with aspirin and clopidogrel on 10/03; dual antiplatelet therapy to continue for 21 days total, then aspirin monotherapy. LDL 142; atorvastatin increased to high intensity. BP permissively elevated first 48 hours, then amlodipine added. Urine drug screen positive for cocaine; patient counseled on cessation and given resources. Smoking cessation counseling provided; nicotine patch started.

Speech therapy evaluation: mild expressive aphasia, improving; safe for regular diet with thin liquids. PT/OT: independent with ambulation, mild right fine-motor deficit; recommend outpatient PT/OT and speech therapy.

Discharge Medications New

Clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily through 10/23/2026 (to complete 21 days of dual antiplatelet therapy), then STOP.
Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily.
Nicotine patch 21 mg/24 hr, apply 1 patch daily; remove and replace with new patch every 24 hours.
Changed

Atorvastatin increased from 20 mg to 80 mg PO nightly.
Continue

Aspirin 81 mg PO daily (continue indefinitely).
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily.
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID with meals.
Stopped

Atorvastatin 20 mg (replaced by 80 mg dose).
Discharge Instructions

Do not drive until cleared by neurology.
Check blood pressure at home once daily and keep a log; goal less than 130/80. Bring log to appointments.
Wear the cardiac monitor continuously for 14 days, then mail it back in the provided envelope.
Outpatient PT, OT, and speech therapy referrals placed; therapy office will call to schedule.
Complete smoking cessation; avoid all illicit substances.
Do not stop aspirin or clopidogrel early unless instructed by neurology.
Fasting lipid panel and liver function tests in 6–8 weeks.
Follow-up

Primary care within 1 week.
Stroke neurology clinic in 2–4 weeks.
Return Precautions Call 911 immediately for any new stroke symptoms (BE FAST): loss of balance, vision changes, facial droop, arm or leg weakness, speech difficulty. Also seek urgent care for: severe headache, bleeding that does not stop, black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, or BP greater than 180/110 with symptoms.

Nursing Teaching

BE FAST stroke signs and calling 911.
Clopidogrel stop date (10/23/2026) vs aspirin continued long term.
Bleeding precautions on dual antiplatelet therapy.
Home BP measurement technique and log.
Nicotine patch use: rotate sites, do not smoke while wearing patch.
Cardiac monitor wear and return.
